title: Why People Remember More From Narrated Visuals (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Why People Remember More From Narrated Visuals
slides.notes: Think about the last time you understood something difficult. Odds are someone showed you a picture while they explained it.

slides.title: Two channels are better than one
bullets: A channel for what we see
A channel for what we hear
slides.notes: We take in information through our eyes and our ears. Show a picture and explain it out loud, and the load is shared.

slides.title: Let the visual show, narration explain
slides.notes: A PDF deck makes readers do everything with their eyes. Narration moves the explaining to audio, and the voice tells viewers where to look and when.

slides.title: What gets in the way of learning
bullets: Reading slide text aloud word for word
Words and pictures out of sync
slides.notes: Narrated visuals aren't automatically good. Don't read your bullets aloud, cut decoration that doesn't teach, and talk about what's on screen, while it's on screen.

slides.title: Before and after: the water cycle
bullets: Headline: Water moves in a loop driven by the sun
Each stage appears as the narration reaches it
slides.notes: The diagram carries the structure. The voice carries the explanation. And the build keeps them in step, so each stage arrives as it's named.
